entries.before: Amazon Bedrock gives you explicit control over whether the prompts and outputs from your inference requests are retained. You can configure data retention in a given AWS Region at the account level or project level, and the setting is enforced consistently across the Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses APIs. The setting is per-Region: it governs every request in the Region where you set it and does not propagate to other Regions. A Region you have not configured remains at inherit and falls back to each model's default.
entries.after:
Amazon Bedrock gives you explicit control over whether the prompts and outputs from your inference requests are retained. You can configure data retention in a given AWS Region at the account level or project level, and the setting is enforced consistently across the Messages, Chat Completions, and Responses APIs, and the InvokeModel and Converse APIs on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. The setting is per-Region: it governs every request in the Region where you set it and does not propagate to other Regions. A Region you have not configured remains at inherit and falls back to each model's default.
Choose the mode that matches your policy. If your policy prohibits retention, choose none. If you accept each model's standard retention, choose default. To use models that require AWS automated review or human review, choose aws_review. Your retention mode and your trusted access program enrollment are separate, and changing one doesn't change the other. Some programs change where Amazon Bedrock stores retained inputs and outputs and who reviews them, so read the program's page before you enroll.

entries.before: Default means the data retention policy of the model applies. There is no change to previous model retention behavior; if ZDR applied previously, then ZDR still applies. Actual retention depends on the model — consult the model's terms for specifics. AWS may retain the data for safety and abuse-prevention purposes. The model provider does not receive it. On the Responses API, store defaults to true and may be set to either value.
entries.after: Default means the data retention policy of the model applies. There is no change to previous model retention behavior. Actual retention depends on the model — consult the model's terms for specifics. AWS may retain the data for safety and abuse-prevention purposes. The model provider does not receive it. On the Responses API, store defaults to true and may be set to either value.

entries.before:
This mode allows your inputs and outputs to be retained for human review by AWS. Review is carried out by AWS within the AWS boundary — the model provider does not review your content, and your content is not shared with the provider. Some model providers require Amazon to conduct human review as a condition of access to their models, and this mode is required for access to those models. If a model does not require human review, AWS will not review your content.
See Amazon Bedrock abuse detection and AWS Service Terms.
entries.after:
This mode allows your inputs and outputs to be retained for automated or human review by AWS, unless a trusted access program changes who reviews them. Review is carried out by AWS within the AWS boundary — the model provider does not review your content, and your inputs and outputs are not shared with the provider. Some model providers require Amazon to conduct human review as a condition of access to their models, and this mode is required for access to those models. If a model does not require human review, AWS will not review your content.
For more information, see Automated review and human review.

entries.before: If you are already set to provider_data_share, you do not need to change anything — it sits above aws_review in the ordering below, so it continues to satisfy every model that requires human review. See Amazon Bedrock abuse detection and AWS Service Terms.

entries.before: AWS reviews content only for models whose provider requires human review. Sharing content with model providers is not supported today, so provider_data_share grants a permission that is not exercised — use aws_review instead.
entries.after: AWS reviews content only for models whose provider requires human review. Sharing content with model providers is not supported today, so provider_data_share grants a permission that is not exercised — use aws_review instead. To learn how Amazon Bedrock reviews your inputs and outputs, who reviews them, and what information the model provider receives, see Automated review and human review.
Your mode sets the most retention that you allow. It doesn't cause Amazon Bedrock to retain inputs and outputs for a model that can process your requests without retention.

entries.before: Projects are specific to the bedrock-mantle endpoint. The Bedrock control plane and Runtime APIs have no project concept, so bedrock-runtime requests cannot be project-scoped.
entries.after:
You can set a data retention mode on a project. Unless the mode is inherit, it takes precedence over your account mode for requests that you send through the project. To create projects and send requests through them, see Projects.
For a project on the bedrock-mantle endpoint, set data_retention on the project.

entries.before:
To invoke models with your desired data retention mode on a bedrock-runtime endpoint, set your account data retention mode in that Region using the Bedrock Control Plane API.
curl -X PUT https://bedrock.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/data-retention \
-H "Authorization: Bearer $AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK" \
-H "Content-Type: application/json" \
-d '{ "mode": "aws_review" }'
Response:
{
"mode": "aws_review",
"updated_at": "2026-06-07T20:19:44.723Z"
}
entries.after:
For a project on the bedrock-runtime endpoint, set dataRetention with UpdateProject, or when you create the project with CreateProject.
aws bedrock update-project \
--project-identifier proj_abcdefghijklmnopqrst \
--data-retention mode=aws_review

To check a project that you use with the bedrock-runtime endpoint, run the following command. The dataRetention field in the response shows the project's mode.
aws bedrock get-project --project-identifier proj_abcdefghijklmnopqrst

Example: Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Fable 5.2 require human review (allowed_modes: ["aws_review", "provider_data_share"]). You must explicitly set your data retention mode to aws_review, or to the legacy provider_data_share, before you can invoke these models. If your effective mode is none or default, these models will be unavailable.
By setting aws_review, you are explicitly instructing us to retain your inputs and outputs so that AWS can perform the human review the model provider requires as a condition of access. Your content is not shared with the model provider. See Amazon Bedrock abuse detection and AWS Service Terms.
entries.after:
Example: Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, and Claude Fable 5.2 require human review (allowed_modes: ["aws_review", "provider_data_share"]).
You must explicitly set your data retention mode to aws_review, or to the legacy provider_data_share, before you can invoke these models, including when your account is enrolled in Anthropic Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) or Anthropic Enterprise Data Controls (EDC). If your effective mode is none or default, or if you haven't set a mode, these models will be unavailable. If your account is approved for ZDR on the model, you can also use none or default.
By setting aws_review, you are explicitly instructing us to retain your inputs and outputs so that AWS can perform the human review the model provider requires as a condition of access. Your content is not shared with the model provider. If a trusted access program that you're enrolled in changes who reviews your inputs and outputs, the program's page describes it.

entries.before: ZDR for Claude models that require data retention is granted to customers who are eligible for the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards program. To find out whether you're eligible, contact your AWS account team or AWS Support. For more information, see Model-specific abuse detection.
entries.after: If you're eligible for Anthropic Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), you can get ZDR for certain Claude models that require data retention. If you enroll in EFS or Anthropic Enterprise Data Controls (EDC) without ZDR, or after your ZDR period ends, Amazon Bedrock retains your inputs and outputs for those models. The program's page describes where Amazon Bedrock stores them, for how long, and who reviews them. For more information, see Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) and Enterprise Data Controls (EDC) for Anthropic models and Model-specific abuse detection.

8.4. Amazon CloudWatch Omni
8.4.1. Amazon CloudWatch Omni ("Omni") enables you to connect third-party products and services, including third-party AI agents (each, a "Third-Party Integration"), to a space you create in Omni. By connecting a Third-Party Integration, you agree and instruct us to send Your Content from that space to the Third-Party Integration's provider and its subcontractors, and to give the provider access to that content as you have configured, including through credentials, roles, or permissions you authorize through Omni, for processing which may be outside of the AWS region in which you use Omni.
8.4.2. Third-Party Integrations are Third-Party Content and are provided to you under a separate agreement between you and the applicable provider. AWS is not responsible for any Third-Party Integration, including the provider's processing of Your Content. AWS may change, discontinue, or deprecate support for a Third-Party Integration at any time. Where practicable under the circumstances, AWS will provide you with prior notice of any deprecation or discontinuation of support for a Third-Party Integration.
8.4.3. Output returned to Omni by a Third-Party Integration is Your Content. Output is provided by the provider, not AWS, and should be evaluated for accuracy as appropriate for your use case, including by employing human review of such output. You and your End Users are solely responsible for all decisions made, advice given, actions taken, and failures to take action based on such output.
8.4.4. You are responsible for providing legally adequate privacy notices to your End Users and obtaining any necessary consents from them for the sharing of Your Content with a provider of a Third-Party Integration.

17. Google Cloud Platform Access Tools.
a. Additional Definitions.
“Access Point” means a Google API, model context protocol (MCP) server,
endpoint, tool interface, connector, proxy, command line interface, or
third-party service that Customer can connect to a Service to allow Customer
to access or obtain data from or in the Service.
“Access Tool” means any AI Agent, AI Harness, software, application,
AI model, service employing an AI model, or other tool that can be used to
obtain or access data via an Access Point.
“AI Agent” has the meaning given in Section 14 (Definitions) under
“AI/ML Services” in the “Service Terms” section below.
“AI Harness” means the software layer that can deploy an AI Agent,
invoke tools or APIs, or orchestrate tasks across one or more AI Agents.
“Google Technical Information” means information related to the
Services obtained or derived from access to or interaction with the Access
Point(s) (including embeddings, memory stores, topology or organization, IAM,
architecture, costs, tool schema, graphs, profiles, summaries, and findings)
or from failure patterns established from calls to Access Points. Google Technical
Information does not include any Customer Data.
“Third-Party Access Tool” means (i) any Access Tool that is (A)
provided or operated by a third party or (B) deployed or executed via a
third-party AI Harness, or (ii) an Unregistered AI Agent.
“Unregistered AI Agent” means an AI Agent that is (i) created or
used by Customer to access an Access Point, and (ii) not deployed via, or
registered with, an Agentic AI Service.
b. Additional Terms. If Customer uses
or authorizes any Access Tool to access or interact with any Access Point,
then the following terms apply:
i. Customer may not engage in any of the activities in subsections (A)
through (F) below:
(A) Store any Google Technical Information for more than 30 days;
(B) Process any Google Technical Information for any purpose other than to
fulfill active, Customer-authorized tasks;
(C) Retain any Google Technical Information after Customer disconnects the
Access Tool or revokes its access to the Access Point(s);
(D) Scrape or perform systematic probing of the Access Point(s), or any skills,
documentation, or outputs, beyond what is required for a Customer-authorized task;
(E) Use any Google Technical Information for model training, fine-tuning,
evaluation dataset building, or model distillation; or
(F) Use any Google Technical Information to develop or improve a product or service
that is similar to any Service.
If Google reasonably believes that the Access Tool
has engaged in any of the activities in subsections (A) through (F) above,
Google may immediately (1) restrict or remove the Access Tool’s access
to the Access Point(s) and corresponding Service(s); or (2) suspend or
terminate Customer’s access to or use of the Access Point(s) or corresponding
Service(s), as necessary in Google’s determination to stop the activity.
ii. Customer acknowledges that there are risks inherent to implementing a
Third-Party Access Tool on an Access Point, including the potential for:
(A) the Third-Party Access Tool training its underlying model(s) on
Customer Data; (B) unauthorized access to Customer Data obtained by or
via the Third-Party Access Tool; and (C) compromise of Customer’s Account
credentials by or via the Third-Party Access Tool, if it obtains or uses them.
Customer agrees that Google will have no responsibility or liability for or
from these or any other acts or omissions of a Third-Party Access Tool.
